paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: nothing is too difficult for the LORD. Sarah is old, she is past the age of childbearing, and she hears she'll have a son. So she laughs to herself. Then the LORD asks, "Is anything too difficult for the LORD?" (Genesis 18:14).

Look at what the LORD does with her laugh. He doesn't walk away, and He doesn't take back His promise. He says it again: at the appointed time He will return, and Sarah will have a son (Genesis 18:14). When Sarah is afraid and says, "I did not laugh," He answers, "No, but you did laugh" (Genesis 18:15). He knew what was in that tent, and He kept His word anyway.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Some promises of God can feel so far off that you chuckle at them with the camera OFF. I've been there. I spent years in a junk drawer, sure my story was over, and then God reached in and called me out. Take heart, because God keeps His promises, even the ones that sound impossible and even when it's years before you see them kept.
